subject: social_science

concepts.title: Concept of Human Capital and People as Resource
concepts.definition: The working segment of a country considered in terms of its skills, technical abilities, and productive capacities that contribute to national output.
concepts.key_idea: Investing in human beings turns population from a liability into a productive economic asset.
question_patterns: What is meant by people as a resource
How does population transform into human capital
Explain the significance of human capital in national output
Why is human resource considered superior to land and physical capital
Describe how investment in human resources yields returns

solution_steps.explain: Human capital formation occurs through targeted expenditure on schooling, vocational training, and healthcare.
Trained and healthy individuals produce higher output and utilize physical capital and land effectively, generating both private earnings and social benefits.

concepts.title: Virtuous and Vicious Cycles in Human Capital Formation
concepts.definition: A developmental pattern where educated parents invest substantially in their children creating positive compounding gains, contrasted with disadvantaged parents perpetuating deprivation.
concepts.key_idea: Sustained family investment in child health and learning creates intergenerational upward mobility.
question_patterns: Compare the life outcomes of Sakal and Vilas
What constitutes a virtuous cycle in human development
How is a vicious cycle formed among disadvantaged families
Why did Japan become a developed country without rich natural resources
Explain the role of parental awareness in child development

solution_steps.explain: Contrast the presence of formal schooling, vocational courses, and medical care in one case with the absence of schooling and medical treatment in another.
Enhanced skills open formal sector opportunities with rising incomes, while lack of training confines labour to low paying traditional work.

concepts.title: Classification of Economic Activities into Three Sectors
concepts.section: Economic Activities by Men and Women
concepts.definition: The categorisation of all output generating activities into primary extraction, secondary manufacturing, and tertiary service provision.
concepts.key_idea: All three sectors jointly contribute goods and services to the Gross National Product.
question_patterns: Classify given occupations into primary secondary and tertiary sectors
What activities are included in the primary sector
Which sector comprises trade transport and communication
Differentiate between secondary and tertiary sectors
How do economic activities add value to national income

solution_steps.action: Examine the nature of the activity
solution_steps.explain: Primary involves direct exploitation of natural resources; secondary involves industrial processing; tertiary involves services supporting production and distribution.

solution_steps.action: Assign the activity to the corresponding sector
solution_steps.explain: Match the specific occupation against sector criteria to determine its exact classification.

concepts.title: Market versus Non-Market Activities and Gender Division of Labour
concepts.section: Economic Activities by Men and Women
concepts.definition: The distinction between tasks performed for remuneration or profit and unpaid tasks performed for self consumption or domestic upkeep.
concepts.key_idea: Unpaid household work by women is excluded from national income calculations due to the non-market nature of domestic chores.
question_patterns: Distinguish between market activities and non-market activities
Why is domestic work done by women not counted in national income
What factors determine the earning of an individual in the labour market
Why are women often paid lower wages compared to men
Identify whether a given task is an economic or non-economic activity

solution_steps.action: Check for remuneration or commercial exchange
solution_steps.explain: If the effort produces goods or services sold for pay or profit, it is a market activity; if it is for domestic self-use, it is non-market.
Only market activities and own-account fixed asset production enter national income aggregates.

concepts.title: Education and Quality of Population
concepts.definition: The development of human knowledge, values, and literacy that improves individual earning potential and strengthens social governance.
concepts.key_idea: Universal elementary education policies like Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan and Mid-Day Meals improve school retention and literacy.
question_patterns: Explain the role of education in human capital formation
What are the major objectives of Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan
How does the Mid-Day Meal scheme improve primary education
Describe the purpose of Navodaya Vidyalayas in rural districts
What steps have been taken by the government to enhance higher education

solution_steps.explain: Locate programs addressing access (Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan), nutrition and attendance (Mid-day meal), or specialized schooling (Navodaya Vidyalaya).
Increased literacy drives higher labour productivity, greater civic engagement, and higher national income.

concepts.title: Health Indicators and Human Development
concepts.definition: The physiological well-being of the population measured through statistical indicators like life expectancy, infant mortality rate, crude birth rate, and crude death rate.
concepts.key_idea: A healthy workforce maximizes output and prevents loss of working potential due to illness.
question_patterns: Define infant mortality rate birth rate and death rate
Why is health considered an indispensable foundation for economic development
How does life expectancy reflect the quality of life
Calculate the change in health indicator over a period
Explain the expansion of health infrastructure in India since independence

solution_steps.action: Find absolute change in indicator value
solution_steps.explain: Subtract the final value from the initial value or vice versa to get the difference
Divide the difference by the initial value and scale to percentage

concepts.title: Unemployment and Workforce Demographics
concepts.definition: A condition in which individuals within the active working age bracket who are seeking employment at prevailing wages cannot secure jobs.
concepts.key_idea: Only individuals aged 15 to 59 years actively seeking paid work are counted in unemployment statistics.
question_patterns: Define the term unemployment
What is the standard working age group in the Indian workforce
Why are children and elderly people not categorized as unemployed
Explain why housewives choosing domestic work are not counted as unemployed
Compute the number of unemployed individuals from labour force and employment data

solution_steps.explain: Deduct the count of employed persons from the total labour force
Divide the unemployed count by the labour force and multiply by 100

concepts.title: Types of Unemployment: Seasonal, Disguised, and Educated
concepts.definition: Distinct forms of joblessness including agricultural off-season idleness, invisible surplus workers on family plots, and educated degree holders lacking suitable jobs.
concepts.key_idea: Disguised unemployment occurs when marginal productivity of surplus workers is zero.
question_patterns: Differentiate between disguised unemployment and seasonal unemployment
What is educated unemployment and why is it prevalent in urban India
How does disguised unemployment occur in the agricultural sector
Calculate the number of surplus disguised workers on a farm
Explain the paradoxical manpower situation in urban labour markets

solution_steps.explain: Subtract the minimum number of workers needed to maintain output from total engaged workers

concepts.title: Consequences of Unemployment and Sectoral Absorption
concepts.definition: The socio-economic costs of joblessness that transform assets into liabilities, increase dependency ratios, and prompt labour migration to secondary and tertiary sectors.
concepts.key_idea: Unemployment increases economic overload and leads to loss of human capital potential.
question_patterns: What are the detrimental economic consequences of unemployment
Why is agriculture the most labour absorbing sector of the Indian economy
How does creation of vocational skills generate new local employment
Explain how unemployment leads to economic overload
Describe the transition of surplus agricultural labour into modern services

solution_steps.explain: Joblessness heightens the reliance of the non-working population on the employed workforce, reducing living standards.
Small scale manufacturing and emerging tertiary fields such as information technology absorb surplus farm workers.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Infant mortality rate declined from {val_initial} in 1951 to {val_final} in 2020. Calculate the absolute decrease and the percentage reduction in IMR.

solution_template.action: Find absolute change in indicator value
solution_template.explain: Subtract the final value from the initial value
Divide difference by initial rate and multiply by 100

worked_examples.question_pattern: If the death rate fell from {val_initial} to {val_final} per thousand, find the percentage drop in the death rate.

solution_template.action: Find absolute change in indicator value
solution_template.explain: Subtract the final death rate from the initial death rate
Compute the drop relative to the initial value

worked_examples.question_pattern: In a town with a total labour force of {labour_force} persons, {employed_count} persons have gainful jobs. Calculate the number of unemployed individuals and the unemployment rate.

solution_template.explain: Subtract employed individuals from the total labour force
Divide unemployed count by total labour force and scale by 100

worked_examples.question_pattern: A region has an active labour force of {labour_force} people of whom {employed_count} are employed. Find the unemployment rate.

solution_template.explain: Deduct employed persons from total labour pool
Express the unemployed share as a percentage of the labour force

worked_examples.question_pattern: An agricultural field engages {total_workers} family members, whereas the actual work only requires {required_workers} workers. Calculate the number of disguised unemployed workers.

solution_template.explain: Subtract required workers from total workers currently active on the plot

worked_examples.question_pattern: A family farm employs {total_workers} persons to cultivate wheat, but optimal production needs only {required_workers} laborers. How many people represent surplus disguised unemployment?

solution_template.explain: Determine the excess workers who do not contribute to additional output
